summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence, with history of gastrojejunal anastomotic ulcer and recurrent epigastric pain, was directly admitted from clinic for epigastric pain with nausea and vomiting after any oral intake. She was treated with continued G-tube feeds, intravenous fluids for dehydration, and antiemetics with symptom improvement; admission labs were unremarkable. By hospital day 2 she returned to baseline tolerance of tube feeds with improved pain and nausea, and gastroenterology evaluated her with a plan to arrange an outpatient upper endoscopy to further assess the etiology. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable on her home regimen with addition of sucralfate and instructions to follow up with surgery clinic and GI for EGD.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
